name: Transition language
controls: How one scene, shot or state hands over to the next: the join between compositions, from invisible cuts to spectacular transformations.
question: How should one scene hand over to the next?
notes: Feel by family. Professional: hard cut, crossfade, push, slide, mask reveal, UI morph, match cut. Playful: card flip, stretch, liquid, object wipe, shape match, page flip, particle. Cinematic: hard cut, dissolve, camera move, zoom-through, match cut, light wipe, flash, luma matte, foreground wipe, parallax. Experimental: glitch, displacement, fragmentation, noise and pixel dissolve, portal, tunnel, infinite zoom. Technical: hard cut, line-draw, pixel dissolve, wipe, split, UI morph, seamless infinite canvas. Luxurious: slow crossfade, dissolve, light wipe, center mask reveal, slow camera move, luma matte. Fast / social: whip, zoom punch, flash, glitch, hard cut on the beat, stretch, push. Confusable pairs: a fade goes to or from a solid color (usually black or white); a crossfade overlaps two images so A and B are briefly superimposed; a dissolve is the film-editing term for the same superimposition, now often used for textured variants (noise or pixel dissolve) where pixels switch rather than blend; many editors use 'crossfade' and 'dissolve' interchangeably. A wipe moves an edge across a stationary frame to replace A with B (neither image moves); a push moves both frames together, B shoving A out; a slide moves only B in over a stationary A (or A out over a stationary B). A match cut joins two shots through a shared action, idea or composition; a graphic match is a match cut where the shared element is purely visual (shape, position, color), and shape match / color match are the specific graphic-match variants. Morph interpolates any shape into another; object morph keeps a recognizable object and turns it into a different object; UI morph turns one interface element into another interface element (button into modal) as a shared-element transition. In HyperFrames, most transitions are built as a short overlap of the outgoing and incoming scene clips with GSAP tweens on clip-path, transform, opacity and SVG masks; keep transitions between 200ms (social) and 1200ms (luxury) and use one transition family consistently per piece, with one signature transition reserved for the key moment.

options.what: An instantaneous switch from one scene to the next with no transitional frames.
options.looks: Frame A, then frame B; the join is invisible if motion or composition carries across.
options.motion: Zero-duration; energy comes from what moves into and out of the cut.
options.use: Nearly everything: montages, beat-synced reels, dev-tool films, editorial pieces.
options.conveys: Confidence, pace, honesty; the default of professional editing.
options.vs: A jump cut cuts within the same shot for a jarring skip; a smash cut is a hard cut between strongly contrasting scenes for shock.
options.prompt: Join scenes with hard cuts: end scene A while elements are still moving (cut on action) and start scene B with its first element already in motion, so energy carries through the cut; place cuts on beats or sentence boundaries. Use zero-duration tl.set() or clip timing, never a tween.

options.what: The outgoing scene fades to a solid color, then the incoming scene fades up from it.
options.looks: A beat of pure black (or white or brand color) between two scenes.
options.motion: Opacity out over 300-600ms, a 0-400ms hold on the color, opacity in.
options.use: Chapter breaks, openings and endings, time jumps, before an end card.
options.conveys: Closure, passage of time, a breath.
options.vs: A crossfade never passes through a solid color; the two images overlap.
options.prompt: Fade scene A's container to a solid color (opacity 1 to 0 over a black or brand-color background) over 400-600ms with sine.inOut, hold the solid color 200-400ms, then fade scene B up over 400-600ms. Use only at chapter breaks.

options.what: Scene A's opacity falls while scene B's rises over the same period, superimposing them briefly.
options.looks: Two images overlap mid-transition; soft, unobtrusive.
options.motion: Overlapping opacity tweens of 300-800ms (longer for luxury).
options.use: Gentle state changes, luxury pieces, photo sequences, calm explainers.
options.conveys: Softness, continuity, calm. Overused it reads as template.
options.vs: Fade dips to a color; dissolve is the film term for the same superimposition and is often used for textured variants. Crossfade is the common NLE/UI term.
options.prompt: Crossfade by overlapping the two scene clips 400-800ms: scene B is stacked above A and tweens opacity 0 to 1 with sine.inOut while A stays at full opacity underneath (avoiding a mid-transition brightness dip); add a 1.02 to 1 scale settle on B so the transition is not opacity only.

options.what: The film-editing term for superimposing A into B over time, conventionally slower and more poetic than a UI crossfade.
options.looks: Long superimposition where both images coexist and forms from A linger over B.
options.motion: Slow overlapping opacity (800-2000ms), often with a light blur or grade shift.
options.use: Title sequences, brand films, documentary, dreamlike memory beats.
options.conveys: Time passing, reflection, poetic connection between images.
options.vs: Crossfade is the same operation in UI speak and usually quicker; noise and pixel dissolves replace blending with per-pixel switching.
options.prompt: Dissolve slowly: overlap scenes by 1000-1600ms, scene B tweening opacity 0 to 1 with sine.inOut above A, with A gently blurring (0 to 4px) and B resolving from 6px to 0; compose A and B so their main shapes coincide and create a momentary double exposure.

options.what: A moving edge travels across the frame, replacing A with B; neither image moves.
options.looks: A hard or soft line sweeps across; B is revealed behind the line.
options.motion: clip-path inset tween on scene B from one side to the other, 400-700ms.
options.use: Editorial pieces, sports graphics, section changes, before/after.
options.conveys: Order, directional progress, a page being turned over.
options.vs: Push moves both frames; slide moves one frame; a wipe moves only the boundary.
options.prompt: Wipe to scene B by tweening its clip-path from inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) (left to right) over 450-700ms with expo.inOut while scene A stays still underneath; optionally lead the edge with a 4-8px accent-color bar moving with it.

options.what: Scene B enters from one edge and physically shoves scene A out the opposite edge; both move together.
options.looks: The two frames travel side by side as one strip.
options.motion: Both containers translate xPercent 100 in sync with an inOut ease over 400-700ms.
options.use: Carousels, feature sequences, app navigation, social slides.
options.vs: Slide moves only B over a still A; wipe moves only an edge.
options.prompt: Push: scene B starts at xPercent 100 and scene A at 0; tween both by -100 simultaneously over 450-650ms with power3.inOut or expo.inOut so B shoves A off the left edge; add 20px motion blur only if the language allows blur.

options.what: Only scene B moves, sliding in over a stationary scene A (or A slides away to uncover a still B).
options.looks: A new panel or card slides over the old one like a sheet, often with a shadow on its leading edge.
options.motion: Single container translates in from an edge, 350-600ms, A optionally dims or recedes slightly.
options.use: UI navigation (sheets, modals), stacked-card narratives, step sequences.
options.conveys: Layering and depth: the new thing sits on top.
options.vs: Push moves both scenes; slide moves one and implies stacking.
options.prompt: Slide scene B over a stationary scene A: B translates from yPercent 100 (or xPercent 100) to 0 over 400-600ms with power3.out, casting a soft 0 -20px 60px shadow on its leading edge, while A scales to 0.96 and darkens 20% to recede.

options.what: The outgoing scene scales down (or up) while the incoming scene scales in, without implying camera travel.
options.looks: A shrinks into a card or to nothing while B grows to fill the frame.
options.motion: Opposed scale tweens (A 1 to 0.85, B 1.1 to 1), 400-700ms, often with clip or radius changes.
options.use: App store promos, feature reveals, card-to-scene transitions.
options.conveys: Focus shift, containment (scene becomes an object).
options.vs: Zoom implies a camera moving toward or away; scale treats scenes as objects resizing in place.
options.prompt: Scale out scene A (scale 1 to 0.85, border-radius 0 to 32px, darkening 30%) while scene B scales from 1.08 to 1 and wipes in with clip-path circle from the center over 500-700ms with power3.inOut.

options.what: A fast push toward the frame (or pull away) that carries into the next scene, implying camera travel.
options.looks: The frame rushes forward, often with motion blur, and lands in the new scene.
options.motion: Scene A scales 1 to 1.5-3 with power4.in, cut, scene B scales 0.7 to 1 or 1.4 to 1 with power4.out; 300-500ms total.
options.use: Social promos, trailers, hype reels, beat drops.
options.vs: Zoom-through flies into a specific element that becomes the next scene; zoom is a generic punch between scenes.
options.prompt: Zoom A toward camera (scale 1 to 2, power4.in, 200ms, optional 8px blur), cut on the peak, and land B from scale 1.4 to 1 with power4.out over 250-350ms; time the cut to a beat.

options.what: The camera zooms into a specific element (a letter, a screen, a dot) until it fills the frame and becomes the next scene.
options.looks: We dive into the O of a word or into a device screen and emerge in the next world.
options.motion: Large scale tween (x10 to x40) on scene A with transform-origin at the target, B revealed inside the target's shape.
options.use: Product films (zoom into screen), logo reveals, macro-to-micro narratives.
options.conveys: Depth, discovery, 'inside this is another world'.
options.vs: Portal frames B through a shaped opening that we pass through; zoom-through uses an existing element as the opening. Infinite zoom repeats this recursively.
options.prompt: Zoom through the target: set scene A's transform-origin to the target element's center, scale A from 1 to 20-40 with expo.inOut over 800-1200ms; scene B is clipped to the target's shape and scales from the target's size to full frame in sync, so the target becomes B's frame.

options.what: Scenes are laid out on one large canvas and the camera pans, tilts or dollies from one to the next.
options.looks: The world is continuous; the next scene is literally next to the previous one.
options.motion: One world container translates (and optionally scales) with inOut eases of 800-1400ms.
options.use: One-take product films, storytelling across a canvas, timelines, maps.
options.vs: Push moves two separate frames; a camera move travels through one continuous space. Seamless infinite canvas is the extended version across a whole film.
options.prompt: Lay out scenes A and B on one oversized world container (e.g. 3840x1080) and move the camera by tweening the world's x/y (and scale 1 to 0.9 to 1 mid-move for a dolly feel) over 900-1300ms with power3.inOut; place a few foreground elements between scenes that move faster for parallax.

options.what: A cut that joins two scenes through a shared action, idea or composition so they feel causally or thematically linked.
options.looks: A spinning coin cuts to a spinning globe; a click in one scene continues as a tap in the next.
options.motion: Action or position continues across the cut at the same speed and direction.
options.use: Brand films, product launches, clever explainers, title sequences.
options.vs: Graphic match relies on pure visual likeness (shape, color, position); a match cut can also match action or meaning.
options.prompt: Match the cut: end scene A mid-action (rotation, movement or gesture) and begin scene B with an analogous object doing the same action at the same frame position, speed and direction; hard cut at the peak of the action.

options.what: A match cut where the link is purely visual: the same shape, size, position or color occupies the frame across the cut.
options.looks: A circular button cuts to a circular planet in the same spot; composition stays anchored while content changes.
options.motion: Hard cut or brief crossfade with an anchored element in identical frame position and size.
options.use: Logo reveals, product films, title sequences, idents.
options.vs: Shape match and color match are specific kinds of graphic match; morph physically interpolates instead of cutting.
options.prompt: Anchor a dominant visual element (same bounding box, position and silhouette) at the join: the last frame of A and first frame of B share it exactly; cut hard or with a 120-200ms crossfade so only the content around the anchor changes.

options.what: A graphic match driven by one shape (circle, square, line) that carries from one scene into another.
options.looks: A dot becomes a pixel becomes a planet; a rectangle card becomes a phone screen.
options.motion: The shape persists and transforms slightly (size, radius) while scenes change around it.
options.use: Explainers, brand identity systems built on a core shape, product films.
options.conveys: Coherence, a design system at work.
options.vs: Morph changes the shape into another shape; shape match keeps the shape and changes its meaning.
options.prompt: Carry one shape across the transition: keep it at the same position, then tween its size and border-radius (e.g. 24px dot to 360px rounded card) over 400-600ms while scene A's context exits and scene B's context enters around it.

options.what: A transition where a dominant color field carries across scenes, often by an object expanding to fill the frame with its color.
options.looks: A red button grows until the screen is red, then the next scene appears on a red background.
options.motion: An element expands (clip-path circle or scale) to full frame, becoming the next scene's background.
options.use: Brand-color-led films, feature sections, social promos.
options.conveys: Brand presence, smoothness, bold graphic energy.
options.vs: Fade dips to a neutral color; color match uses a meaningful color that belongs to both scenes.
options.prompt: Expand a brand-colored element from its position to cover the frame (clip-path circle(0% at x y) to circle(150%)) over 500-700ms with power3.inOut; scene B begins on that exact background color, its content entering over it.

options.what: One shape interpolates continuously into another, carrying the viewer from scene A to scene B.
options.looks: A blob flows into a logo; a square melts into a circle containing the next scene.
options.motion: SVG path or clip-path polygon interpolation, 500-1000ms.
options.use: Logo reveals, identity systems, concept explainers.
options.vs: Object morph turns a recognizable object into another recognizable object; UI morph turns interface elements into other interface elements. Shape match keeps the shape constant.
options.prompt: Morph the dominant shape of scene A into the dominant shape of scene B by tweening an SVG path (equal point counts or MorphSVGPlugin) or a clip-path polygon with matching vertex counts over 600-900ms with power3.inOut; use the morphing shape as the mask for scene B.

options.what: A recognizable object transforms into a different recognizable object that belongs to the next scene.
options.looks: A coffee cup becomes a battery icon; an envelope unfolds into a dashboard.
options.motion: Staged morph: simplify object A into a neutral shape, then build object B from it; 700-1200ms.
options.use: Metaphor-led explainers, product films, brand storytelling.
options.vs: Morph is any shape interpolation; object morph has meaningful objects at both ends and usually passes through an intermediate shape.
options.prompt: Morph object A into object B in two stages: first collapse A's details and simplify it to a neutral silhouette (circle or rounded rect) over 300-400ms, then grow B's silhouette and details from it over 400-600ms; keep the center of mass fixed.

options.what: One interface element expands or reshapes into another interface state, such as a button becoming a modal or a card becoming a detail page.
options.looks: The tapped card grows into the full screen; a search icon stretches into a search bar.
options.motion: FLIP tween of position, width, height and border-radius; content crossfades inside the morphing container.
options.use: App demos, SaaS walkthroughs, UI showcases, Material Design-style container transforms.
options.vs: Morph is abstract; UI morph follows interface logic and keeps the container as a single continuous surface (Material's 'container transform').
options.prompt: Morph the UI element into the next state as one surface: tween its x, y, width, height and border-radius from the source bounds to the destination bounds over 400-600ms with power3.inOut, fading the old content out in the first 30% and the new content in over the last 50%.

options.what: Scene B appears through a shaped mask that opens (circle, rectangle, type, logo) over scene A.
options.looks: A circle iris opens from the center, or scene B shows through giant letters that expand.
options.motion: clip-path or SVG mask scaling from nothing to full frame; 500-900ms.
options.use: Product reveals, logo transitions, editorial openings, luxury pieces.
options.vs: Wipe uses a straight moving edge; mask reveal uses a shape that grows. Luma matte derives the mask from image brightness.
options.prompt: Reveal scene B through a growing mask: tween B's clip-path from circle(0% at 50% 50%) to circle(75% at 50% 50%) over 600-900ms with circ.inOut or expo.inOut, or use B inside an SVG mask of huge type that scales from 1 to 30.

options.what: A transition where the brightness of a third image (ink bleed, smoke, gradient, texture) decides which pixels show scene B.
options.looks: B appears through spreading ink, smoke or organic blotches rather than a clean edge.
options.motion: An animated grayscale texture's threshold sweeps from black to white over 600-1200ms.
options.use: Brand films, fashion, organic and art-directed pieces, title sequences.
options.vs: Mask reveal uses a geometric shape; luma matte uses the luminance of an image, so edges are organic.
options.prompt: Build a luma-matte transition: apply a CSS mask-image of a grayscale gradient or ink texture to scene B with mask-mode luminance, and animate mask-size or mask-position (or an SVG feComponentTransfer threshold on the texture) over 700-1100ms so white areas spread until B is fully visible.

options.what: An object moving across the frame (a card, a bar, a mascot) acts as the wipe edge, revealing the new scene behind it.
options.looks: A giant logo or product flies across; everything after it is the new scene.
options.motion: The object translates across while B's clip-path follows its trailing edge.
options.use: Brand films, social promos, sports packages, mascot-led pieces.
options.conveys: Energy, brand presence, a hidden cut.
options.vs: Foreground wipe uses an element passing close to the camera (often out of focus); object wipe can be any graphic crossing the frame.
options.prompt: Fly a solid object (brand bar, product, card) across the frame over 400-600ms with power3.inOut; tie scene B's clip-path inset to the object's trailing edge (same tween, same ease) so B appears exactly behind it.

options.what: A foreground element passes close to the camera, filling the frame for a moment and hiding the cut.
options.looks: A blurred shape, pillar or dark silhouette sweeps past; we are in the next scene after it.
options.motion: A large, slightly blurred foreground layer crosses fast (250-450ms) with parallax faster than the background.
options.use: Cinematic brand films, 3D-feeling scenes, one-take illusions.
options.conveys: Seamlessness, a physical camera moving through space.
options.vs: Object wipe is a graphic crossing the frame; foreground wipe simulates depth with an out-of-focus near element.
options.prompt: Pass a large foreground shape (dark, blurred 12-20px, 1.5x frame height) across the camera over 300-450ms with power2.inOut; hard cut from A to B while it fully covers the frame; move background layers at one third its speed for depth.

options.what: Scene A turns like a book page around a vertical edge, revealing scene B beneath.
options.looks: A page hinges at the spine with perspective and a soft shadow as it turns.
options.motion: rotationY 0 to -180 around the left edge with perspective 1200-2000px, 600-900ms.
options.use: Editorial, magazine-style, storybook explainers, catalogs.
options.vs: Card flip rotates around the center to show the back of the same object; page flip hinges at an edge to reveal the next page.
options.prompt: Turn scene A like a page: set transform-origin left center, perspective 1600px on the parent, and tween rotationY 0 to -180 over 700-900ms with power2.inOut, with backface-visibility hidden and a gradient shadow sweeping across scene B beneath.

options.what: A card rotates 180 degrees around its center axis to show its back side, which holds the next content.
options.looks: A 3D flip of a card or tile; front and back faces.
options.motion: rotationY 0 to 180 with perspective, 400-700ms, often with an overshoot settle.
options.use: Before/after, reveals, quiz and stats, feature cards, game-like UI.
options.conveys: Reveal, playful discovery, two sides of one thing.
options.vs: Page flip hinges on an edge and moves on; card flip stays in place and shows the reverse.
options.prompt: Flip the card: wrap front and back faces in a container with transform-style preserve-3d and perspective 1200px, back face pre-rotated 180deg with backface-visibility hidden; tween the container's rotationY 0 to 180 over 500-700ms with power3.inOut (or back.out if the language allows overshoot).

options.what: Scene A folds up along one or more creases like paper, uncovering scene B.
options.looks: Panels hinge and fold with shading on each facet; accordion or origami feel.
options.motion: A split into strips, each strip rotating rotationX around alternating edges, 600-1000ms.
options.use: Paper-craft styles, editorial, map reveals, playful product pieces.
options.vs: Page flip is one rigid page; fold has multiple hinged panels.
options.prompt: Fold scene A: slice it into 3-4 horizontal strips (duplicated clips with clip-path inset), give each strip perspective and alternate transform-origins top/bottom, then tween rotationX to plus/minus 90deg with power2.in staggered 60ms, darkening each strip 40% as it folds, revealing B.

options.what: Scene A splits into two or more pieces that slide apart, revealing scene B behind.
options.looks: The frame opens like doors or blinds along clean lines.
options.motion: Two halves translate apart with inOut eases, 500-800ms.
options.use: Tech launches, reveals, comparison setups, before a hero shot.
options.vs: Wipe replaces with an edge; split physically opens scene A into parts.
options.prompt: Split scene A into two halves (two copies clipped with inset(0 50% 0 0) and inset(0 0 0 50%)) and tween them apart to xPercent -50 and 50 over 500-800ms with expo.inOut, revealing scene B scaling from 1.05 to 1 behind them.

options.what: Scene A stretches along the direction of travel as it exits, and scene B snaps back from a stretch as it enters.
options.looks: Elongated, smeared frames for 2-4 frames, like a rubber band snap.
options.motion: scaleX 1 to 3 on exit and 3 to 1 on enter around the edge, 200-400ms.
options.use: Social promos, playful brands, fast transitions between cards.
options.vs: Whip uses directional blur to simulate a fast pan; stretch deforms the scene geometry.
options.prompt: Stretch A out: transform-origin at its trailing edge, tween scaleX 1 to 3 and x -100% with power4.in over 180-250ms; B enters from the opposite side at scaleX 3 snapping to 1 with power4.out or back.out over 250-350ms.

options.what: Scene B floods in as a liquid form with wavy, gooey edges.
options.looks: A wave or blob shape with rounded, dripping edges sweeps across and fills the frame.
options.motion: An SVG path with a wavy leading edge animates across; or a gooey-filtered set of circles merges.
options.use: Beverage and beauty brands, playful apps, social content.
options.vs: Wipe has a straight edge; liquid has an organic, moving waveform edge. Displacement distorts image content instead of masking.
options.prompt: Mask scene B with an SVG path whose leading edge is a sine wave (8-12 points), tween the path's d from off-screen to full coverage over 600-900ms with power3.inOut while animating wave amplitude from 60px to 0 so the edge sloshes and settles.

options.what: Pixels of scene A are pushed around by a displacement map (noise, ripples) until they break into scene B.
options.looks: The image warps, ripples or smears, then resolves as the next scene.
options.motion: SVG feDisplacementMap scale ramps up then down while scenes crossfade at the peak.
options.use: Creative-tech and AI brands, music, experimental reels.
options.conveys: Transformation, instability, the digital becoming fluid.
options.vs: Liquid transition masks with a wavy edge; displacement distorts the image content itself.
options.prompt: Apply an SVG filter (feTurbulence baseFrequency 0.01-0.02 into feDisplacementMap) to both scenes; tween the displacement scale 0 to 120 to 0 over 700-1000ms with sine.inOut, and swap A for B (a 200ms crossfade) at the peak distortion.

options.what: The cut is disguised by a burst of digital corruption: slice offsets, RGB splits and flicker.
options.looks: 3-8 frames of torn horizontal bands and color fringing between A and B.
options.motion: Stepped slice offsets, channel duplicates offset in x, opacity flicker; 150-350ms.
options.use: Cybersecurity, gaming, music, tech launches, social hooks.
options.vs: Pixel dissolve is an orderly per-block replacement; glitch is disordered corruption.
options.prompt: For 150-300ms around the cut, duplicate the frame into 4-6 horizontal clip-path slices offset -40 to 40px with steps(3), add red and cyan copies offset 6px with mix-blend-mode screen, flicker opacity on steps(2), and switch from A to B mid-burst.

options.what: Scene A goes out of focus and scene B comes into focus, like a rack focus.
options.looks: Soft, dreamy defocus through the join.
options.motion: filter blur 0 to 20px on A overlapping B from 20px to 0, 600-1000ms.
options.use: Cinematic films, luxury, memory or transition between moods.
options.vs: Crossfade blends at full sharpness; blur transition changes focus. Whip uses directional blur for speed.
options.prompt: Rack focus between scenes: A tweens filter blur 0 to 20px and scale 1 to 1.04 with power2.inOut over 700ms while B, overlapping by 400ms, resolves from blur 20px and opacity 0 to sharp with power2.out; only use when the motion language permits blur.

options.what: A very fast pan with heavy directional motion blur that carries from A into B.
options.looks: A few frames of horizontal streaks; the cut hides in the blur.
options.motion: Both scenes translate fast (200-350ms) with power4.inOut; horizontal blur at peak velocity.
options.use: Social promos, energetic brand films, travel and sports.
options.vs: Push is controlled and sharp; whip is fast and blurred. Stretch deforms instead of blurring.
options.prompt: Whip: push A and B together by xPercent -100 over 250-350ms with power4.inOut, applying a horizontal-only blur at peak velocity (SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation '40 0' ramped 0 to 40 to 0) so the join is hidden in streaks.

options.what: A brief burst of white (or color) light covers the cut.
options.looks: One to four frames of overexposed white, like a camera flash or impact.
options.motion: Full-frame white layer opacity 0 to 1 to 0 over 100-250ms with the cut at the peak.
options.use: Trailers, hype reels, drops, impacts, reveals.
options.vs: Fade to white holds the color and eases; flash is a sudden spike.
options.prompt: Put a full-frame white layer above both scenes; tween its opacity 0 to 1 in 60-80ms (power4.in) and back to 0 in 120-180ms (power2.out), cutting from A to B at the peak; sync to a hit or drop.

options.what: A band of light sweeps across the frame, blooming over the join between scenes.
options.looks: A soft glowing band or sheen glides across; brightness peaks where A becomes B.
options.motion: A blurred gradient band translates across with mix-blend-mode screen while B is wiped in under it.
options.use: Premium product reveals, luxury, jewelry, automotive, logo reveals.
options.vs: Wipe has a graphic edge; light wipe hides the edge in a glow. Flash is full-frame and instant.
options.prompt: Sweep a soft light band (a 30-40% width linear-gradient transparent-white-transparent, blur 20px, mix-blend-mode screen) across the frame at a 20deg angle over 800-1200ms with power2.inOut, and wipe scene B in with a clip-path inset tied to the band's center.

options.what: A line draws across or around the frame and becomes the boundary or structure of the next scene.
options.looks: A stroke races across, outlines a shape, then the shape fills or opens into scene B.
options.motion: stroke-dashoffset draw 400-800ms followed by a fill or mask reveal.
options.use: Technical explainers, diagram-led films, developer tools, blueprint styles.
options.vs: Wipe reveals with an edge; line-draw constructs the next scene's frame first.
options.prompt: Draw a 2px line (SVG path with stroke-dasharray equal to its length) across or around the frame with stroke-dashoffset to 0 over 400-700ms using expo.inOut; once closed, use the same shape as a clip-path that opens to reveal scene B.

options.what: Scene A disintegrates into particles that disperse, or particles converge to form scene B.
options.looks: Dots or sparks scatter and swirl; forms assemble from dust.
options.motion: Hundreds of small elements with staggered, randomized (seeded) trajectories, 800-1500ms.
options.use: Logo reveals, AI and data products, magical moments.
options.vs: Fragmentation breaks into larger rigid shards; particle uses tiny points.
options.prompt: Replace scene A's key element with 200-600 small dots sampled from its shape (canvas or DOM, seeded positions), scatter them outward with random vectors and power3.out over 800-1200ms, then converge them into scene B's key element with power3.inOut while B's real element takes over at the end.

options.what: Scene A breaks into shards or tiles that fly apart, revealing scene B.
options.looks: Rigid polygons or grid tiles separate, rotate and fall away.
options.motion: Tiles cloned with clip-path polygons, each with its own rotation and trajectory, staggered.
options.use: Bold reveals, gaming, security (breaking through), hype.
options.vs: Particle is fine-grained dust; fragmentation is large rigid pieces. Pixel dissolve replaces tiles in place without motion.
options.prompt: Clone scene A into 12-30 tiles (grid or Voronoi polygons via clip-path), then tween each tile outward from the impact point with rotation plus/minus 60deg and power3.in over 500-800ms, stagger by distance from the impact (stagger from a point), revealing B underneath.

options.what: Scene B replaces scene A block by block in a random or patterned order.
options.looks: A grid of square blocks flipping from A to B like a digital mosaic.
options.motion: Grid of cells, each switching instantly, staggered randomly over 400-800ms.
options.use: Retro and pixel styles, gaming, technical brands, data themes.
options.vs: Noise dissolve uses organic noise thresholds; pixel dissolve uses hard square blocks.
options.prompt: Cover the frame with a grid of 16x9 to 32x18 cells, each a window onto scene B (clip-path per cell or a mask grid); switch each cell from A to B instantly with tl.set, staggered from random (seeded) across 400-700ms.

options.what: Scene B replaces A through an animated noise threshold, so pixels switch in organic clumps.
options.looks: A grainy, crumbly transition; A erodes like sand into B.
options.motion: Noise texture threshold sweeps from 0 to 1 over 600-1000ms.
options.use: Grainy and textured styles, retro print, experimental brand films.
options.vs: Crossfade blends every pixel equally; noise dissolve switches pixels at different times. Luma matte uses an art-directed texture; noise dissolve uses generic noise.
options.prompt: Mask scene B with an SVG filter: feTurbulence noise into feComponentTransfer (discrete or linear table) whose threshold tweens from 0 to 1 over 600-900ms, so B appears in noisy clumps over A; keep grain size 1-3px for a fine erosion.

options.what: An opening appears within scene A showing scene B, and the camera travels through it.
options.looks: A door, circle or shape cut into the frame reveals another world, then expands around us.
options.motion: A shape clip grows while B scales down from zoomed-in, 800-1200ms.
options.use: Storytelling, product worlds, AR/VR themes, narrative explainers.
options.vs: Zoom-through uses an existing element; a portal is a new opening created for the purpose. Tunnel repeats openings in depth.
options.prompt: Open a portal: B is masked to a shape (circle or rounded rect) that appears small at the focus point, then grows to full frame with expo.inOut over 900-1200ms while A scales up behind it (1 to 1.6) and B scales down from 1.3 to 1, selling camera travel through the opening.

options.what: The camera flies through a series of concentric frames or rings that stream past toward the next scene.
options.looks: Nested rectangles or rings rushing outward, like hyperspace or a corridor.
options.motion: Many concentric layers scale up from 0.1 to 5 with stagger and power2.in, 700-1200ms.
options.use: Tech hype, music, gaming, trailers.
options.vs: Portal passes through one opening; tunnel passes many openings in succession.
options.prompt: Stack 8-15 concentric frames (outlined rectangles or rings, or copies of scene A) and scale them from 0.1 to 5 with power2.in, staggered 60ms from the innermost, over 800-1100ms; scene B sits at the vanishing point and scales up to fill the frame as the last ring passes.

options.what: The camera zooms continuously through nested scenes, each hidden inside a detail of the previous one.
options.looks: An unbroken dive: a city in a screen in an eye in a planet; no cuts.
options.motion: Exponential scale on a nested stack, each level handing off seamlessly; long continuous zoom.
options.use: Title sequences, narrative brand films, micro-to-macro stories.
options.vs: Zoom-through dives once into one element; infinite zoom chains the dive through many nested levels.
options.prompt: Nest each scene inside a small detail of the previous one (each level scaled 1/10 and positioned at its detail); animate a single camera scale on the root exponentially (use equal-duration tweens of x10 each with ease none so speed feels constant), swapping in deeper levels as they fill the frame.

options.what: Scene layers move at different speeds during the transition, so foreground travels faster than background, implying depth.
options.looks: A layered world slides past with foreground elements rushing by and background drifting.
options.motion: Layer translations proportional to depth (e.g. 1.6x foreground, 1x midground, 0.4x background), 800-1200ms.
options.use: 2.5D product films, storytelling, landing-page hero loops.
options.vs: Push moves flat frames at one speed; parallax transition moves depth layers at different speeds.
options.prompt: Split both scenes into 3 depth layers; during the transition translate foreground layers by 160% of the move, midground by 100%, background by 40% with power3.inOut over 900-1200ms, so scene B's layers arrive staggered by depth.

options.what: The entire film lives on one infinite canvas and every transition is the camera travelling to the next region.
options.looks: A Figma- or Miro-like workspace or map where scenes sit side by side and the camera flies between them, zooming out and back in.
options.motion: Camera pans with zoom-out-then-in arcs (scale 1 to 0.5 to 1) between regions, 900-1500ms.
options.use: Collaborative and canvas products (Figma, Miro-style tools), system overviews, one-take launch films.
options.conveys: One connected system, orientation, a product with no seams.
options.vs: Camera move is a single pan between two scenes; infinite canvas is a whole-film spatial architecture.
search: one take motion design product film
options.prompt: Place every scene at fixed coordinates on one world container; between scenes animate the camera (world x, y and scale) in an arc: zoom out to 0.5-0.6 while panning, then zoom back to 1 on the next region, total 1000-1400ms with power3.inOut; never cut.
